about: Quiz for the Graph Hops and Ranking lesson. 'a' = index of the right option (0-based). Key: B C A D B B.

questions.q: The walk reaches hop 2, but under rule 7 none of those passages reach the answer model. Where is the problem?
o: In the walk: depth 2 is too short.
In the rank step: hop 0 alone fills all 10 slots before deeper hops are looked at.
In the linker: it finds too few seed concepts.
In the answer model: it ignores deep passages.
questions.f: The walk already returns hops 1 and 2. Rule 7 sorts by hop first, and one seed concept has 38 or more passages, so hop 0 takes every slot. A deeper walk would change nothing.

questions.q: Depth 2, 10 slots, and every hop has plenty of passages. How does the balanced rule split the slots?
questions.f: Hop 0 gets ceil(10 / 3) = 4. Hop 1 gets ceil(6 / 2) = 3. Hop 2 gets the last 3. The ceiling puts the remainder on the lower hops.

questions.q: Hop sizes are 500, 1 and 1. Why does the thesis rule give 8 / 1 / 1 and not 4 / 1 / 1?
o: Backfill: free slots after the quota pass are filled in rule-7 order, so the list still has 10 passages.
Hop 0 has better scores.
The quota formula gives hop 0 eight slots.
The product rule has a bug.
questions.f: Without backfill only 6 slots are used. Backfill fills the 4 free slots from the remaining passages, hop 0 first. The reason is capacity only; the addendum claims no relevance gain.

questions.q: Which system does NOT fix its depth in advance?
o: GRAG (2-hop ego-graphs)
LightRAG (one-hop neighbours)
GraphRAG local search (one hop)
HippoRAG (Personalized PageRank)
questions.f: HippoRAG has no depth limit. PageRank mass falls off with distance, so far nodes get small scores automatically.

questions.q: Why does the thesis keep a fixed depth and a fixed quota, and not let an LLM decide when to stop?
o: An LLM cannot walk a graph.
A confirmatory test needs one rule fixed before the data; a per-question decision adds a second moving part that could differ between arms.
Fixed depth always gives better answers.
LLM calls are not allowed in the product.
questions.f: The H versus Hc comparison must differ only in the edge labels. A stop rule that runs per question could change with the arm and hide the label effect. The product can still try adaptive options.

questions.q: PPR has the stronger multi-hop record. Why does the thesis still walk with a masked BFS?
o: PPR needs an LLM call for every question.
Plain PPR treats every edge type the same; weights per relation would add a tuned parameter, so H vs Hc would no longer test the labels alone.
PPR cannot reach concepts two hops away.
PPR takes minutes per question on a course graph.
questions.f: With a masked BFS, a masked edge is never followed, so the labels are the only difference between H and Hc. PPR needs no LLM and runs in under a second at 100K nodes; it stays a planned later stage.
